59180-rubble-and-roseleaves-and-things-o.title: And Things of That Kind
59180-rubble-and-roseleaves-and-things-o.creator: Unknown
59180-rubble-and-roseleaves-and-things-o.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. tal—or immortal—subject that takes my fancy. I have merely set down here a few wayward notions that have, in the course of my wanderings, occurred to me. But, in self-defense, let me add that these outbursts have been punctuated by whole infinitudes of silence. The silences are eloquently represented by the gaps between the chapters.

arxiv-2007-00695.title: Experience Report: Smuggling a Little Bit of Coq Inside a CAD Development Context (Extended Abstract)
arxiv-2007-00695.creator: Dimitur Nikolaev Krustev
arxiv-2007-00695.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Dimitur Nikolaev Krustev. While the use of formal verification techniques is well established in the development of mission-critical software, it is still rare in the production of most other kinds of software. We share our experience that a formal verification tool such as Coq can be very useful and practical in the context of off-the-shelf software development – CAD in particular – at least in some occasions.

arxiv-2109-02193.title: A well-balanced oscillation-free discontinuous Galerkin method for shallow water equations Thanks: Y. Liu’s research is partially supported by the fellowship of China Postdoctoral Science Foundation No. 2020TQ0343. Thanks: J. Lu’s research is partially supported by NSFC grant 11901213 and Guangdong
arxiv-2109-02193.creator: Yong Liu, Jianfang Lu, Qi Tao, Yinhua Xia
arxiv-2109-02193.description: Abstract . In this paper, we develop a well-balanced oscillation-free discontinuous Galerkin (OFDG) method for solving the shallow water equations with a non-flat bottom topography. One notable feature of the constructed scheme is the well-balanced property, which preserves exactly the hydrostatic equilibrium solutions up to machine error.

arxiv-2202-03936.title: Accelerometer-based Bed Occupancy Detection for Automatic, Non-invasive Long-term Cough Monitoring
arxiv-2202-03936.creator: Madhurananda Pahar, Igor Miranda, Andreas Diacon, Thomas Niesler
arxiv-2202-03936.description: Abstract We present a new machine learning based bed-occupancy detection system that uses the accelerometer signal captured by a bed-attached consumer smartphone. Automatic bed-occupancy detection is necessary for automatic long-term cough monitoring, since the time which the monitored patient occupies the bed is required to accurately calculate a cough rate.

arxiv-2204-01341.title: An Application of Pixel Interval Down-sampling (PID) for Dense Tiny Microorganism Counting on Environmental Microorganism Images Journal: Journal of L a T e X Templates
arxiv-2204-01341.creator: Jiawei Zhang, Xin Zhao, Tao Jiang, Md Mamunur Rahaman, Yudong Yao, Yu-Hao Lin, Jinghua Zhang, Ao Pan, Marcin Grzegorzek, Chen Li
arxiv-2204-01341.description: Abstract This paper proposes a novel pixel interval down-sampling network (PID-Net) for dense tiny object (yeast cells) counting tasks with higher accuracy. The PID-Net is an end-to-end convolutional neural network (CNN) model with an encoder–decoder architecture. The pixel interval down-sampling operations are concatenated with max-pooling operations to combine the sparse and dense features.

arxiv-2204-09943.title: A novel formulation for the evolution of relativistic rotating stars 2022 A novel formulation for the evolution of relativistic rotating stars – E
arxiv-2204-09943.creator: Hirotada Okawa, Kotaro Fujisawa, Nobutoshi Yasutake, Misa Ogata, Yu Yamamoto, Shoichi Yamada
arxiv-2204-09943.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Hirotada Okawa, Kotaro Fujisawa, Nobutoshi Yasutake, Misa Ogata, Yu Yamamoto, Shoichi Yamada. We present a new formulation to construct numerically equilibrium configurations of rotating stars in general relativity. Having in mind the application to their quasi static evolutions, we adopt a Lagrangian formulation of our own devising, in which we solve force balance equations to seek for the positions of fluid elements assigned to the grid points, instead of the ordinary Eulerian formulation.

arxiv-2207-03007.title: A Novel Experimental Search Channel for Very Light Higgses in the 2HDM Type I
arxiv-2207-03007.description: Abstract We present a reinterpretation study of existing results from the CMS Collaboration, specifically, searches for light Beyond the Standard Model (BSM) Higgs pairs produced in the chain decay p ​ p → H SM → h ​ h ​ ( a ​ a ) pp\to H_{\rm SM}\to hh(aa) into a variety of final states, in the context of the

arxiv-2301-01763.title: Statics and Dynamics of non-Hermitian Many-Body Localization
arxiv-2301-01763.creator: József Mák, M. J. Bhaseen, Arijeet Pal
arxiv-2301-01763.description: Abstract Many-body localized phases retain memory of their initial conditions in disordered interacting systems with unitary dynamics. The stability of the localized phase due to the breakdown of unitarity is of relevance to experiment in the presence of dissipation. Here we investigate the impact of non-Hermitian perturbations on many-body localization.

arxiv-2303-00090.title: Uncertainties in experiments on strongly-coupled vacuum field modification of superconductivity and ferromagnetism in solids
arxiv-2303-00090.creator: J. R. Cooper, L. Forró, A. Jánossy
arxiv-2303-00090.description: Abstract We discuss recent experiments in which fine particles of the organic superconductor Rb 3 C 60 or the cuprate superconductor YBa 2 Cu 3 O 6+x are held in a polystyrene film that is spin-coated on to a silicon substrate with or without an intervening gold, or another inert metallic layer.

arxiv-2410-10085.title: NeRF-enabled Analysis-Through-Synthesis for ISAR Imaging of Small Everyday Objects with Sparse and Noisy UWB Radar Data
arxiv-2410-10085.creator: Md Farhan Tasnim Oshim, Albert Reed, Suren Jayasuriya, Tauhidur Rahman
arxiv-2410-10085.description: Abstract Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar (ISAR) imaging presents a formidable challenge when it comes to small everyday objects due to their limited Radar Cross-Section (RCS) and the inherent resolution constraints of radar systems. Existing ISAR reconstruction methods including backprojection (BP) often require complex setups and controlled environments, rendering them impractical for many real-world noisy scenarios.

arxiv-2412-10641.title: On the low frequency flexural band gaps of a metamaterial plate with low porosity
arxiv-2412-10641.creator: Chaitanya Morey, Sundararajan Natarajan, Chandramouli Padmanabhan
arxiv-2412-10641.description: Abstract This paper demonstrates numerically and experimentally that it is possible to tailor flexural band gaps in the low-frequency regime by appropriate choice of cutout characteristics. The finite element method is used to obtain the numerical dispersion relation and band gaps. The influence of the cutout’s shape, size, and location on the band gap is systematically studied.

arxiv-2501-07781.title: Self-similar inverse cascade from generalized symmetries
arxiv-2501-07781.creator: Yuji Hirono, Kohei Kamada, Naoki Yamamoto, Ryo Yokokura
arxiv-2501-07781.description: Abstract We investigate the role of generalized symmetries in driving non-equilibrium and non-linear phenomena, specifically focusing on turbulent systems. While conventional turbulence studies have revealed inverse cascades driven by conserved quantities integrated over the entire space, such as helicity in three spatial dimensions, the influence of higher-form symmetries, whose conserved charges are defined by integration over subspaces, remains largely unexplored.

arxiv-2506-12915.title: PersonaFeedback : A Large-scale Human-annotated Benchmark For Personalization
arxiv-2506-12915.creator: Meiling Tao, Chenghao Zhu, Dongyi Ding, Tiannan Wang, Yuchen Eleanor Jiang, Wangchunshu Zhou
arxiv-2506-12915.description: Abstract With the rapid improvement in the general capabilities of LLMs, LLM personalization, i.e., how to build LLM systems that can generate personalized responses or services that are tailored to distinct user personas, has become an increasingly important research and engineering problem.

europmc-pmc5703947.title: Integrating evolutionary dynamics into treatment of metastatic castrate-resistant prostate cancer.
europmc-pmc5703947.creator: Zhang J, Cunningham JJ, Brown JS, Gatenby RA.
europmc-pmc5703947.description: Abiraterone treats metastatic castrate-resistant prostate cancer by inhibiting CYP17A, an enzyme for testosterone auto-production. With standard dosing, evolution of resistance with treatment failure (radiographic progression) occurs at a median of ~16.5 months. We hypothesize...

pmc-10560734.title: A glycosylation risk score comprehensively assists the treatment of bladder neoplasm in the real-world cohort, including the tumor microenvironment, molecular and clinical prognosis
pmc-10560734.creator: Jinhui Liu, Yunbo He, Weimin Zhou, Zhuoming Tang, Zicheng Xiao
pmc-10560734.description: Background: Bladder cancer is a common urological cancer associated high significant morbidity and mortality rates. Immunotherapy has emerged as a promising treatment option, although response rates vary among patients. Glycosylation has been implicated in tumorigenesis and immune regulation. However, our current comprehensive understanding of the role of glycosylation in bladder cancer and its clinical implications is limited.

pmc-11545594.title: Fecal Bile Acids in Canine Chronic Liver Disease: Results from 46 Dogs
pmc-11545594.creator: Verena Habermaass, Francesco Bartoli, Eleonora Gori, Rebecca Dini, Aurora Cogozzo, Caterina Puccinelli, Alessio Pierini, Veronica Marchetti
pmc-11545594.description: Simple SummarySince bile acids (BAs) represent one of the metabolic joining links between the gut and the liver, fecal concentrations of BAs could be altered in human patients with different kinds of chronic liver diseases (CLDs). In veterinary medicine, scarce literature is available regarding their potential modification during canine CLDs.

pmc-11574118.title: Advancing aluminum-ion batteries: unraveling the charge storage mechanisms of cobalt sulfide cathodes
pmc-11574118.creator: Andrew Grindal, Gisele Azimi
pmc-11574118.description: Rechargeable aluminum-ion batteries (AIBs) stand out as a potential cornerstone for future battery technology, thanks to the widespread availability, affordability, and high charge capacity of aluminum. However, the efficacy of current AIBs on the market is significantly limited by the charge storage process within their graphite cathodes.

pmc-11654654.title: Revolutionizing neurosurgical care: Cost-effective follow-up with social media applications
pmc-11654654.creator: Raana Shahid, Zainab Safdar
pmc-11654654.description: emains glaring. With only 212 trained neurosurgeons nationwide, averaging just one neurosurgeon for every million citizens, Pakistan lags far behind global standards. This deficiency is acutely felt in cases of emergency trauma, particularly those arising from road traffic accidents, which contribute substantially to the country’s neurosurgical caseload.

pmc-11676997.title: Impact of Conventional and Laser-Assisted Machining on the Microstructure and Mechanical Properties of Ti-Nb-Cr-V-Ni High-Entropy Alloy Fabricated with Directed Energy Deposition
pmc-11676997.creator: Ho-In Jeong, Osama Salem, Dong-Won Jung, Choon-Man Lee, Jeung-Hoon Lee
pmc-11676997.description: The high-entropy alloy (HEA) has recently attracted significant interest due to its novel alloy design concept and exceptional mechanical properties, which may exhibit either a single or multi-phase structure. Specifically, refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEA) composed of titanium, niobium, and nickel-based HEA demonstrate remarkable mechanical properties at elevated temperatures.

pmc-12626793.title: Case Report: Extra skeletal Ewing’s sarcoma of mediastinum: clinical experience and literature review
pmc-12626793.creator: Xianwen Hu, Wei Zhao, Ronghua Yu, Dongfeng Pan
pmc-12626793.description: Extraskeletal Ewing sarcoma (EES) is a malignant tumor that arises in soft tissues outside the skeleton. It commonly involves the paravertebral regions, the lower extremities, and the chest wall, with mediastinal involvement being less frequent. Here, we report an 11-year-old male with pathologically confirmed EES occurring in the mediastinum.

pmc-12745890.title: What's in a Name? Not All Mesopredators Are Mesocarnivores
pmc-12745890.creator: Emily K. Madsen, Lucy Eckersley, Jennifer F. Linden, Sandra Lai, Darragh Hare, David W. Macdonald, David Kimaili, Salum Kulunge, Yolanda Mutinhuma, Lisanne Petracca, Betty J. Rono, Lovemore Sibanda, Claudio Sillero‐Zubiri, Jessica Tacey, Femke Broekhuis
pmc-12745890.description: Ecological terms like mesopredator and mesocarnivore have distinct meanings, the former denoting trophic rank, the latter diet composition. Yet these terms are frequently conflated, leading to conceptual ambiguity. We argue for returning to original definitions and advocate for context‐sensitive, precise language to improve clarity and accuracy in scientific communication about fundamental ecological characteristics of species.

pmc-13071365.title: Subjective and Objective Sleep Measures in Patients With Insomnia With and Without Depression
pmc-13071365.creator: Tina Carbonetti, Michal Bechny, Corrado Garbazza, Jana Koprivova, Karolina Janku, Helen Christina Slawik, Annette Beatrix Bruehl, Undine Emmi Lang, Jan Sarlon
pmc-13071365.description: IntroductionObjectively measured sleep duration often diverges from the subjectively perceived sleep duration in patients with insomnia. Although depression is known to affect sleep, little is known about its influence on the discrepancy between subjective and objective sleep measures, which we sought to clarify in this study.

pmc-13385741.title: Robust but independent sex differences in human brain function, structure, and behavior
pmc-13385741.creator: Siyuan Liu, Bridget W Mahony, Ethan T Whitman, Stephen J Gotts, Dustin Moraczewski, Adam Thomas, Alex Martin, Armin Raznahan
pmc-13385741.description: The neurobiological accompaniments of well-established sex differences in human behavior and disease remain unclear — in part due to a lack of large, diverse functional neuroimaging studies. We address this gap using over 700 h of fMRI data across seven tasks from 978 individuals with extensive structural and behavioral measures.

pmc-13405670.title: Early Phase Adaptations in Strength, Muscle Size, and Co-activation Following Resistance Training in Untrained Women
pmc-13405670.creator: Roberts, Jocelyn E. Arnett, Dolores G. Ortega, Justin S. Pioske, Robert W. Smith, Tyler J. Neltner, Richard J. Schmidt, Terry J. Housh
pmc-13405670.description: The present study examined the effects of four days of training on peak torque (PT), muscle thickness (MT), and electromyographic co-activation (Co- Act). Ten untrained women (age=21.6±1.0 years) completed four days of maximal, reciprocal, concentric, isokinetic forearm extension (FE) and flexion (FF) training with six sets of 10 repetitions at 180°·s−1.

pmc-13565060.title: Extraction Process Optimization, Structural Characteristics and Gut Microbiota Metabolism Regulatory Effect of Suillus luteus Alkali-Extracted Polysaccharide
pmc-13565060.creator: Xiao Han, Zhenjia Sun, Decheng Mao, Tian Wang, Wenjie Ding, Haiyu Ji, Yingyu Yang, Bing Han
pmc-13565060.description: Edible fungal polysaccharides have been recognized as low-toxic natural candidates for tumor adjuvant therapy by regulating gut microbiota and host metabolism. This study aimed to prepare an S. luteus alkali-extracted (pH = 9) polysaccharide (SLP9) via optimized extraction and systematically elucidate the anti-tumor effects based on polysaccharide structure, genus-level gut microbiota and fecal metabolomics.
